id.description: Board project id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, unique, not _board. It names the project on its tasks, in the journal and in its source ids such as jira:<id> and github:<id>:<repo>.

type.description: jira: tasks come from the Jira issues jql returns, read with JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN from secrets.env.

baseUrl.description: Jira site URL. https:, or http: only on a loopback host.

jql.description: Jira search whose issues become tasks in To Do. A task whose issue leaves the result is flagged out of filter while it has an open PR or a live session, and is archived otherwise, once Spur, the tracker and every repo have a complete poll since its last change and none of them is blind; a task added or removed by hand is left alone.

items.description: A Jira status name, spelled exactly as in Jira.

doneStatuses.description: Jira statuses that mean done. A task whose issue is in one of them and that has no open PR is archived on the next archive.doneWeekday, once every repo has a complete poll since its last change. Each name must exist in every projectKeys project, or the Jira poll fails with a config error.

items.description: A Jira status name, spelled exactly as in Jira.

readyStatuses.description: Jira statuses that mean ready for development. The board checks only that each name exists in every projectKeys project; the Jira poll fails with a config error otherwise.

projectKeys.description: Keys of this board project's Jira projects, such as PROJ. A PR names its task by one of these keys, and doneStatuses and readyStatuses are checked in each of these projects. A task key such as PROJ-12 belongs to the one board project whose list holds its prefix; an empty list takes every Jira key, and a key that several projects take belongs to none. The Jira poll fails with a config error while the list is empty.

items.description: A Jira project key in capitals, such as PROJ.

type.description: github-issues: tasks come from the open issues of tracker.repo, narrowed by label or milestone when set, read with GITHUB_TOKEN.

repo.description: Repository as owner/name whose open issues become tasks. PRs link to its issues only in this repository, so list it in repos too.

label.description: Only open issues with this label become tasks. Set at most one of label and milestone; with neither, every open issue of tracker.repo becomes a task.

milestone.description: Only open issues in the milestone with this title become tasks. Set at most one of label and milestone; with neither, every open issue of tracker.repo becomes a task.

repos.description: GitHub repositories as owner/name whose PRs the board polls for this project, one source each. A done task is archived only after every listed repository has a complete poll since its last change.

reposWithoutCi.description: Repos from repos that run no CI checks, in any letter case. In a listed repo, a PR whose check list on head is empty passes the Dev gate check condition instead of waiting in Dev. A list of only skipped checks still waits, and red or pending checks still count. A listed repo whose branch protection requires checks that have not reported yet also passes, so list only repos that run no checks. Without this key, a PR with no checks waits in Dev.

items.description: A repository from repos as owner/name, in any letter case.

link.description: How a project links a PR to its task. A github-issues project reads an issue number from PRs in tracker.repo; a Jira project reads an issue key with one of tracker.projectKeys from PRs in repos. Left at the defaults, a Jira project links every tracker.projectKeys key (such as PROJ-12, any letter case) in the PR title or head branch. Set the sources and patterns to the branch and PR title naming rules of the repos. The board does not enforce those rules; the repo enforces them through its CI title check and its agents' skills. board doctor compares these rules with recent PRs by operatorGithubLogin.

sources.description: Where a PR names its task, in priority order; the first source that yields an issue number wins (for a Jira project, an issue key). closing: issues in tracker.repo the PR closes (Closes #12 in the body, or linked in the sidebar), for PRs to the default branch only; a Jira project skips it. branch: branchPattern on the head branch. title: titlePattern on the PR title.

items.description: One place a PR can name its task: closing, branch or title.

branchPattern.description: Regular expression that starts with ^ and whose one capture group reads the issue number from a PR head branch, such as <agent>-<number>-<slug>. Branches longer than 255 characters are not matched. For a Jira project the capture group reads the issue key, such as PROJ-12, which must use one of tracker.projectKeys in any letter case; left at the default, a Jira project finds every such key in the PR head branch.

titlePattern.description: Regular expression that starts with ^ and whose one capture group reads the issue number from a PR title, such as fix(core): #12 summary. Titles longer than 255 characters are not matched. For a Jira project the capture group reads the issue key, such as PROJ-12, which must use one of tracker.projectKeys in any letter case; left at the default, a Jira project finds every such key in the PR title.

operatorGithubLogin.description: The GitHub account agents open PRs under. PR discovery in repos keeps only PRs whose author is this login. It is not necessarily the maintainer's own account: when agents push as one account and a maintainer approves as another, set the agents' account, or no PR is discovered.

spurProjects.description: Spur projects whose sessions work on this board project, each with a role; at most one curator. Board commands from a session whose Spur project is in no spurProjects list are refused.

name.description: The name of the project in Spur. A Spur project can be listed under only one board project.

role.description: worker: sessions of this Spur project may link to this project's tasks through their PR or branch. operator: sessions act as the operator. curator: sessions answer the questions no column orchestrator takes and escalate the rest to the operator; a board project has at most one.

columns.description: The project's board columns in canonical order. todo, dev and done must be present and enabled. A column left out or disabled is skipped. Without this key, all nine columns are enabled with orchestrator none.

id.description: The built-in column this entry configures.

enabled.description: false skips the column: tasks move past it and its exit condition is not checked. todo, dev and done cannot be disabled.

orchestrator.description: Who takes the column's turns. none: the task's live worker session, else the operator. operator: the operator, who also gets the questions asked in the column. Otherwise the name of a spurProjects entry whose sessions orchestrate the column and get the questions others ask in it.

cycleLimit.description: How many times a task may return to Dev from this column before the board stops it for the operator. Returns by the column executor, changes requested and external comments count; a conflict, red CI and a draft do not.

dispatcher.description: How the board moves tasks between columns. The board records the mode it last ran with. The daemon reads the mode at start, so a change takes effect after a restart; a switch from shadow to on copies the shadow column of each task into its column, and a switch back to shadow closes the open turns and starts the shadow column from the column again.

mode.description: shadow: the board evaluates the column gates and records where each task would go in its shadow column, and opens no turn, doorbell or block; the column executor submits with the task key. on: the board moves the task between columns, hands the column executor a turn and raises the cycle-limit block.

projects.description: Board projects, at least one. Each reads tasks from one tracker and PRs from its repos. A Spur project can be listed under only one board project.

slack.description: Slack user ID of the operator, such as U0123456789. Slack commands, button presses and messages from anyone else are denied. A feed line the operator resolves names this user.

appName.description: Slack app and bot display name that board slack manifest writes when --app-name is not given.

command.description: Slash command with its leading slash. The board acts only on this command, and board slack manifest writes it when --command is not given. When slack.channels is set and SLACK_APP_CONFIG_TOKEN and slack.appId are present, board doctor compares it with the installed app.

appId.description: Slack app ID, such as A0123456789. When slack.channels is set and SLACK_APP_CONFIG_TOKEN is present, board doctor reads this app's manifest to check the installed slash command against slack.command.

orchestrators.description: Slack channel ID, such as C0123456789, where the board opens a thread for each block addressed to the operator by someone else. Once either channel is set, the daemon does not start without the other channel and SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, and without SLACK_APP_TOKEN it reads nothing from Slack.

feed.description: Slack channel ID where the board posts a line for each curator answer, each newly installed version and each operator item, with the buttons the operator presses. Operator items about failed Slack posts, transport health, undelivered answers and ended workers, and those shown as operator blocks, get no feed line. A line whose item clears before it is first sent, such as an expired token request, is dropped. Set it together with orchestrators.

staleMultiplier.description: A source with no complete poll for this many of its poll intervals turns blind stale. board status marks that source, and an operator item whose fact is older than that, as stale.

blockOpenMs.description: How long a block may stay open before an item is raised in milliseconds.

doneWeekday.description: Weekday whose local midnight, in digest.tz, is the weekly archive slot: tasks done before it are archived then, once their repos have a complete poll since their last change. A slot missed while the daemon was down is applied on the next tick.

tz.description: IANA time zone, such as Europe/Berlin, for the archive.doneWeekday slot and the times shown in resolved feed lines.

retentionDays.description: Days the board keeps each caller's mutation --key with its input and result. In that time the same caller and key with the same input returns the stored result, and with a different input the call is refused. A daily job deletes older keys.

firstRetryMs.description: Wait after the first unanswered doorbell in milliseconds.

secondRetryMs.description: Wait after the second unanswered doorbell in milliseconds.

unansweredAfterMs.description: Wait after the third unanswered doorbell in milliseconds.

port.description: Local HTTP API port (0 assigns a free port). The default 4777 is above 4310-4399, a margin kept for Spur's server port 4310 and the ports from 4311 upward that its MCP port takes, and avoids Spur's ports 5555 and 8730-8799 and the Linux ephemeral range 32768-60999.

intervalMs.description: Time between two polls in milliseconds.

baseUrl.description: Base URL of the local Spur HTTP API.

intervalMs.description: Time between two polls in milliseconds.
Time between two polls in milliseconds.
Time between two polls in milliseconds.

authRetryMs.description: Wait before polling a source again after an auth error in milliseconds.

goneAfterPolls.description: Complete polls an entity must be missing from before it counts as gone.

reserveRemaining.description: GitHub API requests to leave unused in each quota window.

errorAfterMs.description: How long a session stays in error before it is flagged in milliseconds.

needsInputAfterMs.description: How long a session waits for input before it is flagged in milliseconds.

idleInDevAfterMs.description: How long a worker session without an open PR, or the executor of a taken turn, waits at its prompt before it is flagged in milliseconds.

flipSmoothingMs.description: How long a new session health value must hold before it is reported in milliseconds.

sessions.description: Sessions entering error within the window that start an episode.

windowMs.description: Window in which that many sessions entering error start a host-load episode in milliseconds.

maxEpisodeMs.description: Longest a host-load episode lasts before error flags resume in milliseconds.
